episodes.description: Why can't you see your blind spot? Each of your eyes has an area where it sees nothing, because the optic nerve leaves the eye there and there are no light sensors. Here's how your other eye and your brain cover the gap, and how to find yours: cover your left eye, look at a cross, lean in, and watch a red dot vanish.
episodes.caption: There's a hole in your vision you've never noticed. Here's why, in clay.

episodes.description: Why does metal feel colder than wood when both are the same temperature? Your skin can't measure an object's temperature. It feels how fast its own heat is leaving, and aluminum carries heat over a thousand times better than wood. The ice cube test at the end proves it: the metal melts the ice first.

episodes.description: Where does gold come from? Not from ordinary stars: they can only build atoms up to iron. Gold needs a flood of neutrons within seconds, and one place that happens is when two neutron stars, the crushed cores of dead stars, crash together. Crashes like that seeded the cloud our Sun formed from, so the gold in your ring is older than the Sun.
episodes.caption: The gold in your ring is older than the Sun. Here's the crash that made it, in clay.
